Tarzan: Literary hero raised by apes in the African jungle, known for vine-swinging, great strength, and companion Jane.
Terminator: Relentless cyborg assassin sent through time, usually portrayed in dark sunglasses and associated with protecting or targeting future leaders.
The Devil: Personification of evil and temptation in many religious and folklore traditions, often depicted with horns, red skin, and a pitchfork.
The Genie: Blue magical being from Aladdin who emerges from a lamp, grants three wishes, and performs shape-shifting comic spectacles.
The Invisible Man: Science-fiction character whose experiment makes his body unseen, leaving clothing, bandages, and floating objects as clues to his presence.
The Joker: Batman's chaotic comic-book enemy, recognizable by clown makeup, green hair, a purple suit, and dangerous practical jokes.
The Jolly Green Giant: Towering green mascot who watches over a valley of vegetables and promotes canned and frozen produce.
The Michelin Man: White tire-company mascot built from stacked rubber tires, one of advertising's oldest recognizable characters.
The Professor: Brilliant mastermind from Money Heist who plans elaborate robberies, recruits code-named thieves, and directs operations from hiding.
The Shark: Enormous great white from Jaws whose attacks threaten a beach town and are signaled by an ominous two-note theme.
Thomas Edison: American inventor and businessman associated with the practical light bulb, phonograph, motion pictures, and a prolific patent laboratory.
Thomas the Tank Engine: Cheerful blue number-one locomotive who works on the Island of Sodor and learns lessons with other talking trains.
Thor: Marvel's hammer-wielding god of thunder from Asgard, known for lightning powers, long hair, and membership in the Avengers.
Tiger Woods: American golf superstar known for red shirts on Sundays, numerous major championships, and transforming the sport's popularity.
Tokyo: Impulsive narrator and robber from Money Heist who joins the Professor's crew under a city-based code name.
Tom Brady: Record-setting American football quarterback who won multiple Super Bowls with New England and Tampa Bay.
Tom Cruise: Hollywood action star known for Mission: Impossible, performing dangerous stunts, and a memorable fighter-pilot role in Top Gun.
Tony Montana: Ambitious Cuban immigrant turned Miami crime boss in Scarface, known for lavish excess and explosive confidence.
Tony Soprano: New Jersey mob boss from The Sopranos who attends therapy while balancing criminal leadership and suburban family pressures.
Tony the Tiger: Muscular orange cereal mascot with a red neckerchief who enthusiastically promotes Frosted Flakes.
Toto: Dorothy's small black dog in The Wizard of Oz, who accompanies her from Kansas along the yellow brick road.
Tutankhamen: Young Egyptian pharaoh whose nearly intact golden tomb was discovered in 1922, inspiring worldwide fascination with ancient Egypt.
Ulysses: Roman name for Odysseus, the clever wandering hero who spends ten years returning home after the Trojan War.
Uncle Sam: Bearded personification of the United States, usually wearing stars and stripes and pointing from a famous recruitment poster.
Usain Bolt: Jamaican sprinting legend and world-record holder known for lightning speed and his celebratory lightning-bolt pose.
Victoria Beckham: British singer known as Posh Spice from the Spice Girls who later became a prominent fashion designer.
Vincent van Gogh: Dutch Post-Impressionist painter known for swirling stars, vivid sunflowers, expressive brushwork, and the story of his injured ear.
Voldemort: Noseless dark wizard from Harry Potter who fears death, commands loyal followers, and is linked to Harry by a lightning scar.
Wall-E: Lonely trash-compacting robot left to clean an abandoned Earth who collects treasures and falls for a sleek probe named EVE.
Whoopi Goldberg: American actress, comedian, and television host known for Sister Act, Ghost, and cohosting The View.
Willie Mays: Baseball legend nicknamed the Say Hey Kid, celebrated for power, speed, and an iconic over-the-shoulder World Series catch.
Winnie-the-Pooh: Gentle bear from the Hundred Acre Wood who loves honey and shares simple adventures with Piglet, Tigger, and Christopher Robin.
Winston Churchill: British prime minister who rallied the United Kingdom during World War II, known for cigars, speeches, and a bulldog-like image.
Wolverine: Gruff X-Men hero with retractable metal claws, rapid healing, heightened senses, and a mysterious past.
Woodstock: Tiny yellow bird from Peanuts who communicates in scribbles and serves as Snoopy's loyal, quirky companion.
Woody Allen: American filmmaker known for neurotic comedy, New York settings, and movies such as Annie Hall and Manhattan.
Wyatt Earp: Old West lawman associated with Tombstone, Arizona, and the famous gunfight near the O.K. Corral.
Yoda: Small green Jedi master from Star Wars, known for great wisdom, unusual word order, and powerful command of the Force.
Zelda: Princess of Hyrule from The Legend of Zelda, often connected to wisdom, sacred power, and hero Link's quests.
Zeus: King of the Greek gods who rules from Mount Olympus and wields thunderbolts as his signature weapon.
